To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
universities are able to shape their research profile, and that this is a good thing.

the Dutch state’s authority over research profiles of universities has increased, but universities have considerable operational authority over inclusion and removal of new research fields, and the quasi-market failure of Dutch research is a result of universities’ following the same external signals.

the Dutch state’s interest in research profiles of Dutch university is growing, that the operational authority of university management to shape these research profiles is increasing, and that this may lead to a quasi-market failure in the sense that universities will be unable to provide a broad spectrum of research fields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the consequences of the state’s increased interest in the research profile of Dutch universities, and the role of universities in shaping their research profile.
the consequences of the increasing state interest in research profiles for the autonomy of Dutch universities.
the consequences of universities’ increased autonomy in the context of a changing state interest in the content of research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the Netherlands, the research profiles of Dutch research universities are not shaped by the state but by the university management.
the current Dutch system is a mixed bag.
, while the state has become the dominant authority in the field, university management has become the dominant actor in the process of profile building.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the state has been successful in shaping the research profiles of Dutch university, but at the same time, it has been unsuccessful in creating an environment in which research can be done without state intervention.
the current state of research policy in the Netherlands is a case of ‘too much state, too little market, and too little university’.
, in the current system, universities have a lot to say, but they say the same thing, and this is not necessarily good.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Dutch university model is in danger of being transformed into a market model, in which the state’s role as a regulator of research is reduced to that of an external funding agency.

, while universities are increasingly free to choose their research profile, the freedom is not used to build research profiles based on the best research, but on the basis of the research that can most easily attract external funding.
, in the absence of a strong state interest in a specific profile, the university management’s interest is likely to prevail.
